category: System Variables: Dimensions, Text, Files & Environment
description: The third set of system variables: attribute display, dimension associativity and the dimension-style variables most often overridden (text placement, fit, zero suppression, precision, continue mode), text defaults and fonts, save behaviour, xref defaults, regeneration, startup and single-document mode, code pages and proxies, the MTEXT editor, LISP loading and search paths, menu/status bar, plotting quiet mode, layout regeneration and viewport scaling, drawing identity and modification flags, dates, path prefixes, product identity, annotation monitoring, undo control, user variables, command state, extended names, text editing, command history, thumbnails and tray notifications. Related variables are grouped in each entry.

tools.name: ATTMODE
tools.description: Global attribute visibility: 0 all attributes hidden, 1 (default) each attribute's own Invisible flag is honoured, 2 all attributes shown including invisible ones. ATTDISP is the command that sets it. Attribute creation defaults live in AFLAGS (bit sum of the ATTDEF modes: 1 invisible, 2 constant, 4 verify, 8 preset, 16 lock position, 32 multiple lines), ATTMULTI (allow multiline attributes) and ATTIPE (full in-place editor for multiline attributes).
tools.usage:
ATTMODE = 0 off | 1 normal | 2 on
AFLAGS = bit sum of ATTDEF modes (1 invisible, 2 constant, 4 verify, 8 preset, 16 lock position, 32 multiple lines)
ATTMULTI = 0 | 1 ; ATTIPE = 0 | 1

parameters.name: plotting
parameters.description: Invisible attributes never plot; ATTMODE 2 shows and plots them (used for checking).

tools.example:
ATTMODE 2
(inspect hidden part numbers)
ATTMODE 1
tools.notes: ATTMODE is saved in the drawing and triggers a REGEN. AFLAGS is registry and only affects new ATTDEFs.

tools.name: DIMASSOC
tools.description: Associativity of new dimensions: 2 (default) fully associative to the geometry they measure (they update when it changes, and trans-spatial dimensions in paper space follow model objects), 1 non-associative (one object, measured once), 0 exploded (lines, arrowheads and text as separate objects). Drawings from other CAD systems arrive with 0 or 1; check before dimensioning. DIMREASSOCIATE repairs lost associations and DIMDISASSOCIATE removes them.
tools.usage:
DIMASSOC = 0 exploded | 1 non-associative | 2 associative (default)
OPTIONS > User Preferences > Associative Dimensioning > Make new dimensions associative

parameters.name: annotation monitor
parameters.description: ANNOMONITOR 1 flags dimensions that lost associativity with a badge.

parameters.name: xrefs
parameters.description: Associative dimensions can measure xref geometry; they update on reload (DIMREGEN if needed).

tools.example:
DIMASSOC 2
DIMLINEAR (snap to END of the plate corners) -> stretching the plate updates the dimension
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing. DIMASSOC 0 is set by some legacy CAM/GIS exports; dimensions made with it cannot be re-associated (they are not dimension objects).

tools.name: INSUNITSDEFSOURCE
tools.description: Unit assumed for a source drawing or block that has no INSUNITS (unitless) when it is inserted or dragged in from DesignCenter/the Blocks palette, and INSUNITSDEFTARGET the unit assumed for the current drawing when it is unitless; together with INSUNITS they determine the automatic scale factor applied to inserted content (mm into inches = 1/25.4). OPTIONS > User Preferences > Insertion Scale exposes both.
tools.usage:
INSUNITSDEFSOURCE = 0 unspecified (no scaling) | 1 inches | 2 feet | 4 millimetres | 5 centimetres | 6 metres ... (same codes as INSUNITS)
INSUNITSDEFTARGET = same codes
INSUNITS = unit of the current drawing (1 inches, 4 millimetres, 6 metres...)

parameters.name: scaling rule
parameters.description: Scale = source unit / target unit, applied to INSERT, XATTACH, IMAGEATTACH, PASTECLIP between drawings and DesignCenter drags; 0 on either side disables scaling.

parameters.name: block libraries
parameters.description: Save library DWGs with the correct INSUNITS so they insert at the right size everywhere.

tools.example:
INSUNITS 4
INSUNITSDEFSOURCE 1   ; unitless legacy blocks are treated as inches and scaled by 25.4 on insert
tools.notes: Registry settings (INSUNITS itself is per drawing). Unexpected 25.4 scale factors on insertion are almost always these three variables.

tools.name: TEXTSIZE
tools.description: Default height for new single-line text created with TEXT when the current text style has a height of 0 (variable height); it is also the height offered to LISP routines and used by some Express Tools. A style with a fixed height ignores it. TEXTSTYLE names the current style, and TEXTJUSTIFY (2014+) the default justification for TEXT.
tools.usage:
TEXTSIZE = height in drawing units (default 0.2 / 2.5)
TEXTSTYLE = current style name
TEXTJUSTIFY = Left | Center | Right | Align | Middle | Fit | TL ... BR

parameters.name: annotative styles
parameters.description: For annotative styles TEXTSIZE is the paper height; the model height is TEXTSIZE x scale factor.

parameters.name: DTEXT / -TEXT
parameters.description: Prompt 'Specify height <TEXTSIZE>' appears only when the style height is 0.

tools.example:
TEXTSIZE 2.5
TEXTJUSTIFY MC
-TEXT (pick point) Enter 0 ROOM 101
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing. TEXT stores the last used height back into TEXTSIZE. Fixed-height styles make scripting simpler but prevent height changes per object.

tools.name: TEXTFILL
tools.description: Controls whether TrueType text is filled (1, default) or outlined (0) when plotted and rendered; TEXTQLTY sets the tessellation resolution of TrueType outlines for plots (0-100, default 50); QTEXTMODE (Quick Text) replaces all text with rectangles on screen and plot to speed up regeneration of text-heavy drawings; HIDETEXT decides whether text participates in HIDE. TEXTFILL 0 was the classic way to get thin outline lettering for pen plotters.
tools.usage:
TEXTFILL = 0 outlines | 1 filled (default)
TEXTQLTY = 0-100 (default 50; higher = smoother, larger plot files)
QTEXTMODE = 0 | 1 (REGEN to apply)
HIDETEXT = 0 | 1

parameters.name: PDF export
parameters.description: Filled TrueType text is exported as text (searchable) when the driver supports it; outlines become geometry.

tools.example:
QTEXTMODE 1
REGEN
(work fast on a 50,000-text drawing)
QTEXTMODE 0
REGEN
tools.notes: TEXTFILL/TEXTQLTY are registry; QTEXTMODE and HIDETEXT are saved in the drawing. Do not plot with QTEXTMODE 1 by mistake - text plots as boxes.

tools.name: ISAVEPERCENT
tools.description: Amount of wasted space allowed in a DWG file (as a percentage of file size) before a full save is forced; 50 (default) makes most saves incremental and fast, 0 forces a complete save every time (slower but smallest files and fewer corruption risks on flaky networks). ISAVEBAK controls whether a .bak is written (0 speeds saves of huge files), SAVEFIDELITY whether annotative objects are saved with visual fidelity for pre-2008 releases (adds anonymous blocks), and INDEXCTL whether layer/spatial indexes are written for demand loading of xrefs.
tools.usage:
ISAVEPERCENT = 0-100 (default 50)
ISAVEBAK = 0 | 1 (default 1)
SAVEFIDELITY = 0 | 1 (default 1)
INDEXCTL = 0 none | 1 layer index | 2 spatial index | 3 both
SAVEFORMAT is not a variable - the default save version is OPTIONS > Open and Save > Save as

parameters.name: full save
parameters.description: Also forced by SAVEAS to another name/version, by AUDIT/RECOVER and by WBLOCK.

parameters.name: PURGE and file size
parameters.description: An incremental save does not reclaim space; ISAVEPERCENT 0 plus PURGE gives the smallest file.

tools.example:
; CAD standard for issued drawings
ISAVEPERCENT 0
-PURGE A * N
AUDIT Y
QSAVE
tools.notes: ISAVEPERCENT, ISAVEBAK and SAVEFIDELITY are registry; INDEXCTL is saved in the drawing. Incremental saves are one reason DWG sizes creep up until a full save.

tools.name: XREFTYPE
tools.description: Default reference type offered by XATTACH/-XREF: 0 Attachment (nested xrefs come along when this drawing is itself referenced) or 1 Overlay (nested xrefs are not carried into further hosts - the safer default for background drawings that reference each other). BINDTYPE decides how -XREF Bind renames dependent symbols: 0 Bind style (SITE$0$WALL) keeps everything unique, 1 Insert style merges same-named layers/styles like INSERT would.
tools.usage:
XREFTYPE = 0 Attach | 1 Overlay
BINDTYPE = 0 Bind (prefixed names) | 1 Insert (merged names)

parameters.name: circular references
parameters.description: Overlay avoids 'circular reference' errors when A references B and B references A.

parameters.name: ETRANSMIT bind
parameters.description: The transmittal setup's Bind option uses BINDTYPE too.

tools.example:
XREFTYPE 1
BINDTYPE 1
-XREF B *
tools.notes: Both registry settings. Insert-style binding is what most deliverable workflows want (clean layer names); bind-style keeps the audit trail of which xref a layer came from.

tools.name: XEDIT
tools.description: Set in a drawing, controls whether that drawing may be edited in place with REFEDIT when it is attached as an xref elsewhere (1 yes, 0 no) - a way for a discipline to protect its background from being changed by other teams. XREFNOTIFY sets the change notification (0 none, 1 balloon, 2 balloon and status icon) and XREFCTL whether an .xlg log of xref activity is written next to the host drawing.
tools.usage:
XEDIT = 0 no in-place editing of this drawing when referenced | 1 allowed (default)
XREFNOTIFY = 0 | 1 | 2 (default 2)
XREFCTL = 0 no log | 1 write <drawing>.xlg

parameters.name: XREFREGAPPCTL
parameters.description: 2018+: 0 does not copy RegApp records from xrefs into the host (avoids bloat).

parameters.name: XLOADPATH / XLOADCTL
parameters.description: Demand loading behaviour, see XLOADCTL.

tools.example:
; in the structural background drawing
XEDIT 0
QSAVE
tools.notes: XEDIT is saved in the drawing that will be referenced, not the host. XREFNOTIFY and XREFCTL are registry.

tools.name: REGENMODE
tools.description: Whether the drawing regenerates automatically when needed (1, REGENAUTO ON, default) or asks first (0, REGENAUTO OFF - only for enormous legacy drawings where a regen took minutes). WHIPARC displays circles and arcs as true curves (1) rather than vectors (0), and RTREGENAUTO (2021+) governs automatic regens during real-time zoom/pan. These are display-quality vs speed trade-offs alongside VIEWRES.
tools.usage:
REGENMODE = 0 (REGENAUTO OFF) | 1 (REGENAUTO ON)
WHIPARC = 0 vectors | 1 true circles
RTREGENAUTO = 0 | 1
tools.example:
REGENMODE 1
WHIPARC 1
tools.notes: REGENMODE is saved in the drawing. With hardware acceleration the historical cost of regens is small; leave REGENMODE 1.

tools.name: STARTUP
tools.description: Controls what appears when AutoCAD starts or a new drawing is created: 0 no Start tab, a new drawing opens directly; 1 the legacy Startup and Create New Drawing dialogs (wizards, templates, start from scratch); 2 the Start tab (default); 3 the Start tab plus a new drawing. STARTMODE separately shows/hides the Start tab, and SDI 1 forces single-document mode where only one drawing can be open (needed by a few old ObjectARX apps).
tools.usage:
STARTUP = 0 | 1 | 2 (default) | 3
STARTMODE = 0 | 1
SDI = 0 multiple documents (default) | 1 single document interface

parameters.name: QNEW template
parameters.description: With STARTUP 0/2 the QNEW default template decides units and settings of the new drawing.

parameters.name: SDI restrictions
parameters.description: SDI 1 disables the Blocks palette's multi-document features and some LISP document functions.

tools.example:
STARTUP 0
SDI 0
tools.notes: Registry settings. The Core Console ignores them. STARTUP 1 is the only way to reach the old Advanced Setup wizard.

tools.name: DWGCODEPAGE
tools.description: Read-only code page stored in the drawing (e.g. ANSI_1252 Western, ANSI_932 Japanese, ANSI_1251 Cyrillic) used to interpret 8-bit text in SHX-font strings and legacy files; SYSCODEPAGE is the operating system's code page. Since 2007 DWG text is stored as Unicode, so these matter mainly for old drawings whose text shows as garbage: open them on a system with the matching code page or convert with the migration tools. The DXF header variable $DWGCODEPAGE carries the same value.
tools.usage:
DWGCODEPAGE = "ANSI_1252" (read-only; set by the drawing's origin)
SYSCODEPAGE = current system code page (read-only)
DXF: $DWGCODEPAGE in the HEADER section

parameters.name: Big fonts
parameters.description: Asian SHX big fonts (STYLE > Use Big Font) map multi-byte codes; FONTMAP can substitute them.

parameters.name: Unicode escapes
parameters.description: \U+XXXX in text strings is code-page independent.

tools.example:
DWGCODEPAGE -> "ANSI_1252"
SYSCODEPAGE -> "ANSI_1252"
tools.notes: A drawing with DWGCODEPAGE different from SYSCODEPAGE shows a warning on open in older releases. LISP strings from (getstring) are in the system code page on pre-2024 releases; LISPSYS 1/2 in 2021+ switches to Unicode-aware LISP.

tools.name: PROXYGRAPHICS
tools.description: Whether images (graphics) of custom objects are saved in the drawing (1, default) so that AutoCAD without the object enabler can still display them as proxies, or not (0, smaller files but proxies show as nothing/bounding boxes). PROXYSHOW controls how proxies display (0 not shown, 1 graphics, 2 bounding box), PROXYNOTICE whether the 'proxy objects present' dialog appears on open, and DEMANDLOAD when object enablers/ARX apps are loaded on demand (0 never, 1 on open, 2 on command, 3 both). Together they explain why AEC/Civil/Plant drawings look different on plain AutoCAD.
tools.usage:
PROXYGRAPHICS = 0 | 1
PROXYSHOW = 0 no display | 1 graphics (default) | 2 bounding box only
PROXYNOTICE = 0 | 1 (default 1)
DEMANDLOAD = 0 off | 1 load on open | 2 load on command | 3 both (default)

parameters.name: object enablers
parameters.description: Free downloads that let plain AutoCAD display and (partly) edit vertical-product objects; DEMANDLOAD must allow loading.

parameters.name: EXPORTTOAUTOCAD / PURGEAECDATA
parameters.description: Explode proxies or strip AEC data for recipients without enablers.

tools.example:
PROXYNOTICE 0
PROXYSHOW 1
DEMANDLOAD 3
tools.notes: PROXYGRAPHICS is saved in the drawing (set by the authoring product); the others are registry. Proxies cannot be edited without the enabler; EXPLODE turns a proxy into plain geometry when its graphics exist.

tools.name: DIMTAD
tools.description: Vertical position of dimension text relative to the dimension line: 0 centred (line broken), 1 above, 2 outside (away from the object), 3 JIS, 4 below (2010+). It is the Text placement > Vertical setting of DIMSTYLE and pairs with DIMJUST (horizontal: 0 centred, 1 next to first extension line, 2 next to second, 3/4 over the extension lines), DIMTIH/DIMTOH (text horizontal when inside/outside the extension lines vs aligned with the dimension line) and DIMGAP (gap between text and line, negative draws a box around the text). Set with DIMOVERRIDE for individual dimensions.
tools.usage:
DIMTAD = 0 centered | 1 above | 2 outside | 3 JIS | 4 below
DIMJUST = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
DIMTIH / DIMTOH = 0 aligned with dimension line | 1 horizontal (ISO uses 0/0, ANSI mechanical often 1/1)
DIMGAP = distance (negative = boxed text, used for basic dimensions)

parameters.name: ISO style
parameters.description: DIMTAD 1, DIMTIH 0, DIMTOH 0, DIMGAP 0.625 mm at DIMSCALE 1.

parameters.name: style overrides
parameters.description: Typing DIMTAD 1 at the prompt creates a style override affecting new dimensions until DIMSTYLE saves or clears it.

tools.example: DIMOVERRIDE DIMTAD 4 (select the two dimensions below the object)
tools.notes: All DIM* variables are saved in the drawing as the current style's override set. Consult the DIMSTYLE dialog's tooltip to see which variable a control maps to.

tools.name: DIMTIX
tools.description: Forces dimension text between the extension lines even when it does not fit (1) or lets it move outside (0, default) - the Fit tab's 'Always keep text between ext lines'. Its companions: DIMSOXD suppresses the dimension line outside the extension lines when text is forced inside, DIMTOFL draws a dimension line between the extension lines even when the text/arrows are outside (needed for ISO radius dimensions), DIMATFIT decides what moves outside first (0 text and arrows, 1 arrows, 2 text, 3 best fit), DIMTMOVE how text moves when dragged (0 with the line, 1 with a leader, 2 freely) and DIMUPT lets the user place text manually. These are the variables behind crowded-dimension fixes.
tools.usage:
DIMTIX = 0 | 1
DIMSOXD = 0 | 1
DIMTOFL = 0 | 1
DIMATFIT = 0 text+arrows outside | 1 arrows first | 2 text first | 3 best fit (default)
DIMTMOVE = 0 dim line moves with text | 1 leader added | 2 text moves freely
DIMUPT = 0 | 1 (user positions text during creation)

parameters.name: radius/diameter
parameters.description: DIMTOFL 1 with DIMTIX 0 gives a dimension line inside a circle with the text outside (ISO); DIMTIX 1 keeps text inside.

parameters.name: DIMTXTDIRECTION / DIMTXSTY / DIMTXT
parameters.description: Text direction (right-to-left), text style and height of dimension text.

tools.example:
DIMTOFL 1
DIMTIX 0
DIMDIAMETER (pick the circle) (drag outside)
tools.notes: Saved with the style/overrides in the drawing. Grip-moving the text is quicker than changing DIMTMOVE for one-off cases.

tools.name: DIMZIN
tools.description: Zero suppression of primary linear dimension values: bit-coded so 0 suppresses none, 4 suppresses leading zeros (.50), 8 trailing zeros (0.5 not 0.500), 12 both; values 1-3 handle feet-and-inches (1 suppress 0 feet and 0 inches, 2 include both, 3 include 0 feet). It goes with DIMDEC (decimal places), DIMLFAC (linear scale factor applied to measured values, e.g. 25.4 to show inches on a mm drawing, negative to apply only in paper space), DIMRND (rounding increment), DIMDSEP (decimal separator character) and DIMLUNIT (unit format). Angular suppression uses DIMAZIN and DIMADEC.
tools.usage:
DIMZIN = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 (feet-inches) | 4 leading | 8 trailing | 12 both
DIMDEC = 0-8 ; DIMADEC = angular precision ; DIMAZIN = angular zero suppression (0-3)
DIMLFAC = factor (default 1; negative = paper space only)
DIMRND = rounding value (0 none) ; DIMDSEP = "." | "," ; DIMLUNIT = 1 scientific | 2 decimal | 3 engineering | 4 architectural | 5 fractional | 6 Windows desktop

parameters.name: DIMLFAC and viewports
parameters.description: Dimensions in paper space measuring model geometry use the viewport scale automatically (DIMASSOC 2), so DIMLFAC is rarely needed today.

parameters.name: alternate units
parameters.description: DIMALT, DIMALTF, DIMALTD, DIMALTZ, DIMAPOST for dual mm/inch dimensioning.

tools.example:
DIMDEC 1
DIMZIN 8
DIMDSEP ,
DIMRND 0.5
tools.notes: Saved with the style. Rounding (DIMRND) affects the displayed text only; the measured value is unchanged, which is why DIMRND on structural drawings needs a note.

tools.name: DIMCONTINUEMODE
tools.description: Decides whether a continued or baseline dimension (DIMCONTINUE / DIMBASELINE / DIM Continue) inherits the dimension style and layer of the dimension it continues from (1, default since 2014) or uses the current style and layer (0). With 1, chains stay consistent even when the current style changed; with 0 old macros that expected the current style keep working.
tools.usage: DIMCONTINUEMODE = 0 use current style/layer | 1 inherit from the selected dimension (default)

parameters.name: DIMLAYER
parameters.description: A fixed dimension layer overrides the layer part of this behaviour.

tools.example:
DIMCONTINUEMODE 1
DIMLINEAR ... 
DIMCONTINUE (select the last dimension; continue picking)
tools.notes: Registry setting. Introduced in 2014 to fix chains with mixed styles.

tools.name: MTEXTED
tools.description: Names the editor used for MTEXT: Internal (the in-place editor, default) or the path of an external text editor (e.g. notepad) for plain-text editing of multiline text, with the ability to chain both (Internal;notepad). MTEXTTOOLBAR controls the text formatting toolbar (0 none, 1 toolbar, 2 ribbon contextual tab), MTEXTCOLUMN the default column mode (0 none, 1 dynamic, 2 static), MTEXTFIXED the editor display (2: fixed height/orientation in the editor), MTJIGSTRING the placeholder text shown while placing (default 'abc'), MTEXTAUTOSTACK automatic stacking of fractions and MTEXTEDENCODING (2022+) the encoding expected from the external editor.
tools.usage:
MTEXTED = "Internal" | "<path to editor>" | "Internal;<editor>" | "OldEditor" (legacy dialog, older releases)
MTEXTTOOLBAR = 0 | 1 | 2 (default 2)
MTEXTCOLUMN = 0 no columns | 1 dynamic | 2 static (default 2 in recent releases)
MTEXTFIXED = 0 | 1 | 2 (default 2)
MTJIGSTRING = up to 10 characters (default "abc")
MTEXTAUTOSTACK = 0 | 1 ; MTEXTDETECTSPACE = 0 | 1 ; MTEXTEDENCODING = ANSI | UTF-8 | UTF-16

parameters.name: external editor
parameters.description: Edits the raw MTEXT string with formatting codes; useful for bulk paste from other tools.

parameters.name: TEXTEDITMODE
parameters.description: 1 makes TEXTEDIT repeat automatically for the next object.

tools.example:
MTEXTED Internal;notepad
(MTEXT opens the in-place editor; Ctrl+... or the editor's menu opens Notepad)
MTEXTCOLUMN 0
tools.notes: All registry settings. MTEXTCOLUMN 2 (static) on by default surprises users who paste long text and get a column break; set 0 for single-column notes.

tools.name: FONTALT
tools.description: Alternate font used when a text style's font file cannot be found (default simplex.shx); FONTMAP names the font mapping file (acad.fmp) whose lines 'missingfont;replacement' substitute specific fonts - the way to make drawings from other offices display with your fonts, or to force TrueType to SHX for plotting speed. Missing SHX fonts prompt on open unless a mapping exists; missing TrueType fonts fall back silently to Windows substitution.
tools.usage:
FONTALT = "simplex.shx" | any font file on the support path
FONTMAP = "acad.fmp" | path to a .fmp file
acad.fmp line format:  romans;simplex.shx   (font name without extension ; replacement font file)
OPTIONS > Files > Text Editor, Dictionary, and Font File Names > Alternate Font File / Font Mapping File

parameters.name: mapping precedence
parameters.description: FONTMAP entries apply even when the original font exists (they are forced substitutions); FONTALT only when a font is missing.

parameters.name: eTransmit
parameters.description: Include fonts in transmittals to avoid substitution on the receiving end.

tools.example:
; acad.fmp
romand;romans.shx
arial;arial.ttf
FONTMAP C:/std/office.fmp
REGEN
tools.notes: Both registry settings; the .fmp is re-read on REGEN/open. Substituted fonts have different widths, so text may overflow title-block cells.

tools.name: ACADPREFIX
tools.description: Read-only string listing the support file search path folders separated by semicolons - what (findfile), fonts, linetypes, hatch patterns, LISP autoload and menu loading search. Related environment variables: ACADLSPASDOC (0 acad.lsp loads once per session, 1 once per drawing like acaddoc.lsp), LISPINIT (in SDI mode, reinitialise LISP for each new drawing), LISPSYS (2021+: 0 classic Visual LISP/VLIDE, 1 or 2 the VS Code environment with Unicode LISP, controlling which compiler MAKELISPAPP uses), LEGACYCODESEARCH (whether the drawing's own folder and the start-in folder are searched for executables - a security setting) and the trusted paths (TRUSTEDPATHS, SECURELOAD).
tools.usage:
ACADPREFIX = "C:\Users\...\Support;C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2025\Support;..." (read-only)
ACADLSPASDOC = 0 | 1
LISPINIT = 0 | 1 (SDI only)
LISPSYS = 0 Visual LISP (VLIDE) | 1 VS Code, Unicode LISP, .fas/.vlx compiled for the new engine | 2 VS Code with legacy ASCII behaviour
LEGACYCODESEARCH = 0 (default; only trusted/support paths) | 1 (also the current drawing folder and start-in folder)

parameters.name: (findfile "x.lsp")
parameters.description: Searches ACADPREFIX folders and returns the full path or nil.

parameters.name: startup order
parameters.description: acad.rx, acad2025.lsp, acad.lsp, acad2025doc.lsp, acaddoc.lsp, the MNL of loaded CUIx files, then Startup Suite (APPLOAD) and bundles.

tools.example:
; LISP: is the office library on the path?
(if (findfile "office_tools.lsp") (load "office_tools") (alert "office_tools.lsp not on the support path"))
; VS Code environment
LISPSYS 1
tools.notes: ACADPREFIX is per profile (OPTIONS > Files > Support File Search Path); the /s switch appends folders for a session. Changing LISPSYS requires a restart and affects how compiled FAS/VLX files must be built.

tools.name: MENUBAR
tools.description: Shows the classic pull-down menu bar (File, Edit, View...) above the ribbon (1) or hides it (0, default) - the menus come from the CUIx Menus section. MENUECHO suppresses echo of menu macro input on the command line (bit sum), STATUSBAR (2015+, 0/1) hides the application status bar, and LAYOUTTAB (2015+) toggles the Model/Layout tabs along the bottom edge. They are the remaining knobs of the 'classic' look besides workspaces and toolbars.
tools.usage:
MENUBAR = 0 | 1
MENUECHO = bit sum: 1 suppress echo of menu items | 2 suppress system prompts during menu | 4 disable ^P toggling | 8 debug (display DIESEL input/output)
STATUSBAR = 0 | 1
LAYOUTTAB = 0 | 1

parameters.name: ^P in macros
parameters.description: Toggles MENUECHO bit 1 inside a macro so the macro's typed commands are not shown.

parameters.name: MENUCTL
parameters.description: Whether the screen menu / menu bar switches pages with command context (legacy).

tools.example:
MENUBAR 1
LAYOUTTAB 1
STATUSBAR 1
tools.notes: All registry settings except LAYOUTTAB which is registry too. The status bar's contents (which toggles appear) are chosen from its Customization menu, not by variables.

tools.name: PLQUIET
tools.description: Suppresses non-fatal plot dialogs and error messages during batch plotting and scripts (1) - e.g. the 'plot style table not found' or 'paper size not available' notices become command-line messages instead of modal boxes. It pairs with BACKGROUNDPLOT (0 foreground, mandatory for scripts), FULLPLOTPATH (send the full path or only the file name to the plot spooler), PLOTOFFSET (offset origin: printable area or paper edge), PLOTROTMODE (how rotation applies) and PLOTTRANSPARENCYOVERRIDE (plot transparency behaviour).
tools.usage:
PLQUIET = 0 dialogs shown | 1 quiet (script mode)
BACKGROUNDPLOT = 0 foreground | 1 background plot | 2 background publish | 3 both (default 2)
FULLPLOTPATH = 0 file name only | 1 full path (default 1)
PLOTOFFSET = 0 lower-left of printable area | 1 lower-left of paper
PLOTROTMODE = 0 rotate about the lower-left corner | 1 rotate and align lower-left corner | 2 (default) rotate the paper image
PLOTTRANSPARENCYOVERRIDE = 0 | 1 | 2

parameters.name: Core Console
parameters.description: Runs effectively with PLQUIET semantics; still set BACKGROUNDPLOT 0 so the console waits for the plot before exiting.

parameters.name: PLOTOFFSET
parameters.description: Explains why the same offset lands differently on plotters with different margins; use 1 for consistent sheet alignment.

tools.example:
; batch plot prelude
PLQUIET 1
BACKGROUNDPLOT 0
FULLPLOTPATH 1
PLOTOFFSET 1
tools.notes: PLQUIET, BACKGROUNDPLOT and FULLPLOTPATH are registry; PLOTOFFSET and PLOTROTMODE are saved in the drawing. Fatal plot errors still stop a script.

tools.name: LAYOUTREGENCTL
tools.description: Controls how display lists are cached for the Model tab and layouts to trade memory for speed when switching tabs: 0 regenerate on every switch, 1 (default) cache the Model tab and the last layout, 2 cache all tabs. LAYOUTCREATEVIEWPORT decides whether a new layout gets an automatic viewport (1, default) or starts empty (0 - preferred for template-driven work), PAPERUPDATE whether a warning appears when a layout's paper size does not fit the plotter or the layout silently updates, and PSVPSCALE sets the default scale of new viewports (0 = scaled to fit).
tools.usage:
LAYOUTREGENCTL = 0 | 1 | 2
LAYOUTCREATEVIEWPORT = 0 no viewport | 1 create a viewport in new layouts (default)
PAPERUPDATE = 0 warn | 1 update paper size silently
PSVPSCALE = 0 scaled to fit | scale factor (e.g. 0.01 for 1:100)
MVIEWPREVIEW = 0 | 1 preview when inserting a viewport (2019+)

parameters.name: memory
parameters.description: LAYOUTREGENCTL 2 with dozens of layouts uses a lot of RAM; 1 is the balance.

tools.example:
LAYOUTCREATEVIEWPORT 0
PSVPSCALE 0.02
LAYOUT N A1-02
(then MVIEW at exactly 1:50)
tools.notes: All registry settings. PSVPSCALE gives new MVIEW viewports a fixed scale so they are not 'scaled to fit' and later forgotten.

tools.name: VPROTATEASSOC
tools.description: When a layout viewport is rotated with ROTATE, decides whether the view inside rotates with it (1, default since 2010 - so a rotated site plan viewport shows north-up geometry rotated correctly) or the view stays fixed and only the frame rotates (0, the legacy behaviour). VPCOORDS (2020+) shows the model-space coordinates under the cursor when a viewport is active in a layout, and VPMAXIMIZEDSTATE reports VPMAX.
tools.usage:
VPROTATEASSOC = 0 view not rotated | 1 view rotates with the viewport (default)
VPCOORDS = 0 paper coordinates | 1 model coordinates when in a viewport

parameters.name: DVIEW twist
parameters.description: Rotating the view sets the viewport's VIEWTWIST; text in model space appears rotated on the sheet, so annotate in paper space or use annotative text with 'Match orientation to layout'.

tools.example:
VPROTATEASSOC 1
ROTATE (pick the viewport frame) (base point) 30
tools.notes: Registry setting. Rotating viewports is the clean way to present skewed sites; the alternative is UCS + PLAN inside the viewport, which VPROTATEASSOC automates.

tools.name: DWGTITLED
tools.description: Read-only: 1 if the current drawing has been given a name (saved at least once), 0 for an unnamed Drawing1 - scripts and LISP test it before QSAVE, which would otherwise open the Save As dialog. DBMOD reports what has changed since the last save (bit sum: 1 object database, 4 database variables, 8 window, 16 view, 32 field), DWGCHECK controls the 'drawing was last saved by another application / opened by another user' warnings, and DWGNAME/DWGPREFIX give the file name and folder.
tools.usage:
DWGTITLED = 0 | 1 (read-only)
DBMOD = bit sum (read-only; 0 = unmodified)
DWGCHECK = 0 no check | 1 alert when a drawing was last saved by a non-Autodesk application | 2 also warn on command line for drawings from other users (default 2) | 3 ...
DWGNAME / DWGPREFIX (read-only)

parameters.name: LISP save guard
parameters.description: (if (= 1 (getvar "DWGTITLED")) (command "_.QSAVE") (command "_.SAVEAS" "2018" "C:/out/new.dwg"))

parameters.name: DBMOD in reactors
parameters.description: A save reactor can skip work when DBMOD is 0.

tools.example:
(if (and (= 1 (getvar "DWGTITLED")) (/= 0 (getvar "DBMOD")))
  (command "_.QSAVE"))
tools.notes: DBMOD is cleared by a save; opening a drawing that needs a recover sets bits immediately. DWGCHECK is registry.

tools.name: CDATE
tools.description: Current date and time as a real in calendar format YYYYMMDD.HHMMSSmm (read-only), convenient for LISP timestamps; DATE holds the same moment as a Julian day number with fractional day (used for elapsed-time arithmetic), MILLISECS (2018+) the milliseconds since Windows started (for timing code), and TDCREATE/TDUPDATE/TDINDWG/TDUSRTIMER the drawing's creation, update, editing and user-timer values in Julian form (with TDUCREATE/TDUUPDATE in UTC).
tools.usage:
CDATE = 20250927.14350812 (read-only)
DATE = 2460946.6 (Julian day, read-only)
MILLISECS = integer (read-only)
TDCREATE / TDUPDATE / TDINDWG / TDUSRTIMER / TDUCREATE / TDUUPDATE (read-only Julian values)

parameters.name: formatting
parameters.description: (menucmd "m=$(edtime,$(getvar,date),DD-MO-YYYY HH:MM)") formats DATE with DIESEL from LISP; fields use %<\AcVar Date \f "dd/MM/yyyy">%.

parameters.name: timing
parameters.description: (setq t0 (getvar "MILLISECS")) ... (- (getvar "MILLISECS") t0) measures a routine in ms.

tools.example:
(setq stamp (rtos (getvar "CDATE") 2 6))   ; "20250927.143508"
(setq s (menucmd "m=$(edtime,$(getvar,date),YYYY-MO-DD HH:MM:SS)"))
tools.notes: CDATE's fractional part is not a decimal time - parse it as digits. DATE's integer part changes at midnight UTC-adjusted local time; use TDUCREATE for cross-time-zone comparisons.

tools.name: LOCALROOTPREFIX
tools.description: Read-only path of the local (non-roaming) user profile folder for AutoCAD (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2025\R25.0\enu\), where caches, templates cache and the graphics cache live; ROAMABLEROOTPREFIX is the roaming folder (%APPDATA%\...) holding Support, plot styles, plotters, CUIx and tool palettes; MYDOCUMENTSPREFIX is the user's Documents folder; TEMPPREFIX the temporary folder (OPTIONS > Files > Temporary Drawing File Location) used for autosave and xref copies; SAVEFILEPATH the autosave folder. LISP uses them to write user files in the right place.
tools.usage:
LOCALROOTPREFIX / ROAMABLEROOTPREFIX / MYDOCUMENTSPREFIX / TEMPPREFIX / SAVEFILEPATH (read-only strings ending with a backslash)
Plotter and plot style folders have no system variable: read them with (getenv "PrinterConfigDir") and (getenv "PrinterStyleSheetDir") (OPTIONS > Files > Printer Support File Path)

parameters.name: (getenv)
parameters.description: Many path settings without a system variable are readable with (getenv "ACAD") (support path), (getenv "PrinterStyleSheetDir") (CTB folder), (getenv "TemplatePath").

parameters.name: deployment
parameters.description: Enterprise support content is best placed on a network path added to ACADPREFIX rather than in the roaming folder.

tools.example:
(setq cfg (strcat (getvar "ROAMABLEROOTPREFIX") "Support\\office.cfg"))
(setq tmp (strcat (getvar "TEMPPREFIX") "scratch.txt"))
tools.notes: All read-only. The folder names contain the release number (R25.0 for 2025, R25.1 for 2026), so code must not hard-code them.

tools.name: PROGRAM
tools.description: Read-only identity of the running application: PROGRAM ("acad"), PRODUCT ("AutoCAD", "AutoCAD LT", "AutoCAD Architecture"...), PLATFORM ("Microsoft Windows NT Version 10.0 (x64)"), _PKSER (serial number), _VERNUM (internal build string, e.g. "V.154.0.0 AutoCAD 2025"), ACADVER ("25.0s (LMS Tech)"), LOGINNAME (Windows user) and STARTINFOLDER/WORKINGFOLDER (2016+). LISP and .NET add-ins read them to branch by product, version and user, and CAD managers put them into plot stamps and title-block fields.
tools.usage: PROGRAM = "acad" ; PRODUCT = product name ; PLATFORM = OS string ; _PKSER = serial ; _VERNUM = build ; ACADVER = "25.0s ..." ; LOGINNAME = user name ; STARTINFOLDER / WORKINGFOLDER = paths  (all read-only)

parameters.name: LT detection
parameters.description: (wcmatch (getvar "PRODUCT") "*LT*") - useful because LT lacks many commands even though it runs LISP since 2024.

tools.example:
(if (< (atof (getvar "ACADVER")) 24.0)
  (alert "This tool needs AutoCAD 2020 or later"))
(princ (strcat "\nUser: " (getvar "LOGINNAME")))
tools.notes: ACADVER's suffix letter (s) indicates the localisation/build; compare numerically. _PKSER shows the serial only for perpetual licences; named-user subscriptions may return a generic value.

tools.name: ANNOMONITOR
tools.description: Turns the annotation monitor on (1), off (0) or on only while an annotation-affecting command runs (2, default since 2013): it badges dimensions, leaders and centre marks that lost their associativity and shows a status-bar icon with a link to re-associate. Its neighbours: SELECTIONANNODISPLAY (show the other scale representations faded when an annotative object is selected), ANNOTATIVEDWG (whether the drawing itself behaves as an annotative block when inserted), CANNOSCALEVALUE (read-only numeric value of the current annotation scale, 0.02 for 1:50) and MSLTSCALE/PSLTSCALE for linetype scaling by annotation scale.
tools.usage:
ANNOMONITOR = 0 off | 1 on | 2 on during annotation commands (default)
SELECTIONANNODISPLAY = 0 | 1 (default 1)
ANNOTATIVEDWG = 0 | 1 (only settable when the drawing has no annotative objects)
CANNOSCALEVALUE = real (read-only; 1 / scale denominator)

parameters.name: badges
parameters.description: A yellow exclamation badge near a dimension means it is disassociated; right-click > Re-associate.

parameters.name: scale math
parameters.description: Model text height = paper height / CANNOSCALEVALUE; e.g. 2.5 / 0.02 = 125.

tools.example:
ANNOMONITOR 1
(stretch the plate without osnaps; the dimension shows a badge)
DIMREASSOCIATE D
tools.notes: ANNOMONITOR and SELECTIONANNODISPLAY are registry; ANNOTATIVEDWG is saved in the drawing. The monitor slows very large drawings slightly when set to 1.

tools.name: UNDOCTL
tools.description: Read-only bit code describing the UNDO state: 1 undo enabled, 2 single-level only (UNDO Control > One), 4 auto-group mode on (each command is one undo step), 8 a group is currently active (UNDO BEgin was issued), 16 combine zoom/pan (UNDO Control > Combine), 32 layer property changes combined. UNDOMARKS (read-only) is the number of marks placed with UNDO Mark. LISP routines that wrap many commands in (command "_.UNDO" "_BE") ... ("_.UNDO" "_E") or (vla-StartUndoMark doc) read UNDOCTL to avoid nesting groups.
tools.usage:
UNDOCTL = bit sum (read-only): 1 enabled | 2 one-level | 4 auto | 8 group active | 16 combine zoom/pan | 32 combine layer changes
UNDOMARKS = count (read-only)
UNDO command: Auto / Control [All/None/One/Combine/Layer] / BEgin / End / Mark / Back / number

parameters.name: group guard
parameters.description: (if (zerop (logand 8 (getvar "UNDOCTL"))) (command "_.UNDO" "_BE")) before a routine; end the group only if this routine started it.

parameters.name: ActiveX
parameters.description: (vla-StartUndoMark doc) / (vla-EndUndoMark doc) - the same grouping without the command.

tools.example:
(defun c:BATCHFIX ( / doc)
  (setq doc (vla-get-ActiveDocument (vlax-get-acad-object)))
  (vla-StartUndoMark doc)
  ;; ... many edits ...
  (vla-EndUndoMark doc)
  (princ))
tools.notes: UNDO Control None disables undo and frees memory for giant batch jobs, at the cost of OOPS/undo. Undo groups left open (bit 8) at the end of a LISP routine make the next U undo more than expected.

tools.name: USERI1
tools.description: Five integer (USERI1-USERI5), five real (USERR1-USERR5) and five string (USERS1-USERS5) variables reserved for user and third-party use: the integer and real ones are saved in the drawing, the string ones are not (session only). They are a lightweight way to pass values between LISP routines, scripts and macros, or to store a per-drawing setting without xdata or a dictionary - but any application may use them, so treat them as scratch space.
tools.usage:
USERI1..USERI5 = integer (saved in drawing)
USERR1..USERR5 = real (saved in drawing)
USERS1..USERS5 = string (not saved)
(setvar "USERR1" 2.5) (getvar "USERR1")

parameters.name: DIESEL
parameters.description: $(getvar,users1) in a menu macro or MODEMACRO reads the string values, the classic way to show a custom status.

parameters.name: alternatives
parameters.description: For durable per-drawing data use (dictadd)/(vlax-ldata-put) (Xrecords) or DWGPROPS custom properties; for user settings use (setcfg)/(vl-registry-write).

tools.example:
; script sets a value that a later LISP reads
USERR1
0.02
; LISP
(setq sc (getvar "USERR1"))
tools.notes: Being shared, two add-ins using USERI1 for different purposes clash silently. Values survive QSAVE but USERS* are lost on reopen.

tools.name: CMDACTIVE
tools.description: Read-only bit code showing what is currently active: 1 an ordinary command, 2 a transparent command, 4 a script, 8 a dialog box, 16 a dynamic data exchange (DDE), 32 an AutoLISP routine, 64 an ObjectARX command. CMDNAMES (read-only) lists the active command names (e.g. "LINE" or "ZOOM'LINE" for a transparent zoom inside LINE), and ERRNO holds the code of the last AutoLISP error condition (e.g. 52 = entity selection failed, 7 = invalid function argument...). LISP uses them to know whether it was called from a script, whether a command is in progress before calling (command), and to diagnose errors.
tools.usage:
CMDACTIVE = bit sum (read-only)
CMDNAMES = "COMMAND" | "OUTER'INNER" (read-only)
ERRNO = integer (read-only in effect; reset with (setvar "ERRNO" 0))

parameters.name: reactor safety
parameters.description: In a command reactor, test (getvar "CMDNAMES") to react only to specific commands; never call (command) from a reactor callback.

parameters.name: script detection
parameters.description: (logand 4 (getvar "CMDACTIVE")) non-zero means a script is running - skip interactive prompts.

tools.example:
(if (/= 0 (logand 1 (getvar "CMDACTIVE")))
  (princ (strcat "\nA command is active: " (getvar "CMDNAMES")))
  (command "_.REGEN"))
tools.notes: CMDNAMES includes the leading underscore/hyphen variants as typed ("-LAYER"). ERRNO codes are listed in the AutoLISP Developer's Guide (Error codes table).

tools.name: EXTNAMES
tools.description: Sets the naming rules for symbol-table names (layers, blocks, styles, linetypes...): 1 (default since 2000) allows extended names up to 255 characters including spaces and most special characters; 0 restricts names to the R14 rules (31 characters, no spaces, limited characters) - required when a drawing must be saved to R14 or exchanged with systems that reject long names. Saved in the drawing.
tools.usage: EXTNAMES = 0 R14 naming (31 chars, A-Z 0-9 $ - _ only) | 1 extended names (255 chars, spaces allowed; not < > / \ " : ; ? * | , = `)

parameters.name: SAVEAS R14
parameters.description: AutoCAD truncates/renames long names when saving to R14 DXF regardless; setting EXTNAMES 0 first lets you control the names.

tools.example:
EXTNAMES 0
-LAYER N A-WALL-EXTR  (rejected: too long) ...
tools.notes: Changing EXTNAMES to 0 in a drawing that already has long names does not rename them. Modern exchange (DXF 2000+) supports extended names.

tools.name: TEXTEDITMODE
tools.description: Makes TEXTEDIT (and double-click text editing) repeat automatically so that after finishing one text object the command immediately prompts for the next (1), or run once (0, default before 2017). TEXTGAPSELECTION (2021+) lets text be selected by clicking in the gaps between its characters, and TEXTALLCAPS / TEXTAUTOCORRECTCAPS (2015+) convert new text to uppercase or fix Caps-Lock typing. Together they tune the text-editing loop for annotation-heavy work.
tools.usage:
TEXTEDITMODE = 0 single | 1 repeat (default 1 in current releases)
TEXTGAPSELECTION = 0 | 1 (default 1)
TEXTALLCAPS = 0 | 1
TEXTAUTOCORRECTCAPS = 0 | 1 (default 1)

parameters.name: TEXTEDIT Mode option
parameters.description: TEXTEDIT M Single/Multiple sets the same behaviour per run.

tools.example:
TEXTEDITMODE 1
TEXTEDIT (pick note 1, edit, click outside; pick note 2 ...) Esc
tools.notes: Registry settings. TEXTALLCAPS applies to TEXT and MTEXT input and attribute values typed in the editor, not to pasted text or fields.

tools.name: CMDINPUTHISTORYMAX
tools.description: Number of previous command-line inputs kept for recall with the Up/Down arrows and the recent-input shortcut menu (default 20, 0-999), and INPUTHISTORYMODE a bit code deciding where that history is offered: 1 in the command line (arrows), 2 in the shortcut menu (Recent Input), 4 recent input for the current command in the shortcut menu, 8 markers for recent points in the drawing area (default 15). Raising the history helps when re-entering long file paths; disabling the point markers declutters the screen.
tools.usage:
CMDINPUTHISTORYMAX = 0-999 (default 20)
INPUTHISTORYMODE = bit sum: 1 arrows at the command line | 2 Recent Input in the shortcut menu | 4 current-command recent input | 8 recent-point markers (default 15)

parameters.name: Recent Input
parameters.description: Right-click during a prompt > Recent Input lists values typed for that kind of prompt (distances, points, names).

tools.example:
CMDINPUTHISTORYMAX 100
INPUTHISTORYMODE 7
tools.notes: Registry settings. History is per session; it is not written to the log file.

tools.name: THUMBSIZE
tools.description: Resolution of the thumbnail preview saved in the DWG for the Open dialog, Explorer, the Start tab and sheet set/DesignCenter previews: 0 = 64x64, 1 = 128x128, 2 = 256x256 (default), up to 8 = 2560x2560; THUMBSAVE (0/1) controls whether a preview is saved at all, THUMBSIZE2D (2018.1) whether 2D wireframe previews follow THUMBSIZE, and UPDATETHUMBNAIL a bit code deciding which thumbnails (sheet views, model views, sheets) are updated when and whether a preview is generated for the current drawing (bit 8) or by the Sheet Set Manager. Larger thumbnails mean larger files and slower saves.
tools.usage:
THUMBSIZE = 0-8 (64 px .. 2560 px; default 2 = 256)
THUMBSAVE = 0 no thumbnail | 1 save (default)
THUMBSIZE2D = 0 | 1
UPDATETHUMBNAIL = bit sum: 1 sheet view thumbnails | 2 model view thumbnails | 4 sheet thumbnails | 8 update when views are created/edited/restored | 16 update when the drawing is saved (default 15)

parameters.name: current view
parameters.description: The thumbnail is the view at the time of saving; zoom to a meaningful view before the final QSAVE.

parameters.name: Core Console
parameters.description: No display means thumbnails may be blank unless the script sets a view and the console regenerates it.

tools.example:
THUMBSIZE 4
ZOOM E
QSAVE
tools.notes: Registry settings. Sheet set thumbnails are stored in the .dst / drawing views; the Windows Explorer preview needs the DWG thumbnail handler shipped with AutoCAD or DWG TrueView.

tools.name: TRAYICONS
tools.description: Shows (1, default) or hides (0) the system tray area at the right of the status bar where notification icons appear (xref changes, plot/publish complete, standards violations, Autodesk account, updates); TRAYNOTIFY (0/1) controls whether the balloon notifications pop up and TRAYTIMEOUT how many seconds they stay (0 = until closed, 1-10). CAD managers turn balloons off on plotting workstations and scripts avoid them altogether with the Core Console.
tools.usage:
TRAYICONS = 0 | 1
TRAYNOTIFY = 0 | 1
TRAYTIMEOUT = 0-10 seconds (default 0)
OPTIONS > System > General Options / Display > Status bar tray settings

parameters.name: per-feature notifications
parameters.description: XREFNOTIFY, DATALINKNOTIFY, STANDARDSVIOLATION, PLOT and PUBLISH 'job complete' balloons each have their own switch as well.

tools.example:
TRAYNOTIFY 1
TRAYTIMEOUT 5
tools.notes: Registry settings. Hiding the tray also hides the plot/publish job status link; use the Plot and Publish Details dialog (VIEWPLOTDETAILS) instead.
